https://telex.hu/kulfold/2026/08/05/az-o.text: Menü Kereső Az oroszok ballisztikus rakétákkal támadták Kijevet, legalább 15 ember meghalt az ukrán főváros térségében Külföld Lángoló raktár Kijev közelében Oroszország légicsapása után 2026. augusztus 5-én kora reggel – Fotó: Roman Pilipey / AFP Pál Tamás Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Oroszország az elmúlt éjszaka során nagyszabású ballisztikus rakéta- és dróntámadást hajtott végre Ukrajna fővárosa ellen. A támadássorozatban legalább 15 ember meghalt, több mint ötvenen megsérültek, miközben Kijevben és az ukrán főváros környékén több helyen is tüzek csaptak fel – közölték az ukrán hatóságok. Az ukrán légierő tájékoztatása szerint Oroszország 24 ballisztikus és négy hiperszonikus rakétát, valamint 115 Sahed típusú drónt indított Ukrajna ellen szerdára virradóan. A rakéták közül egyet sem sikerült elfogni – írta a Kyiv Independent portál. A kijevi területen eddig 14 halálos áldozatról és 27 sérültről tudni – közölte az ukrán katasztrófavédelem, hozzátéve, hogy a mentési munkálatok még mindig tartanak. Vitalij Klicsko kijevi polgármester közlése szerint a fővárosban egy ember meghalt, 24-en pedig megsérültek. A sérültek közül 15 embert kórházba szállítottak, közülük négynek válságos az állapota. A Kijev környéki Brovari, Bucsa és Fasztiv járásokban is jelentős károk keletkeztek: raktárépületek és járművek gyulladtak ki az orosz támadások következtében. A kijevi katonai közigazgatás szerint a fővárosban több mint hét helyszínen keletkeztek károk, köztük a Holoszijivszkij, Obolonszkij, Desznyanszkij és Szvjatosinszkij kerületekben. Klicsko korábban arról számolt be, hogy a Holoszijivszkij kerületben két embert sikerült kimenteni egy összeomlott raktár romjai alól. A kutató-mentő munkálatok továbbra is zajlanak, és elképzelhető, hogy még többen rekedtek a romok alatt. Az Obolonszkij kerületben egy rakéta becsapódása után kigyulladt egy húszemeletes lakóház. Kijevben tartózkodó újságírók szerint az első nagy erejű robbanások helyi idő szerint nem sokkal éjfél után, 0:20 körül hallatszottak. Ekkor több ballisztikus rakéta is becsapódott a városban. A robbanások ezután mintegy egy órán keresztül folytatódtak. Ez idő alatt az ukrán légierő többször is figyelmeztetett arra, hogy újabb ballisztikus rakéták tartanak Kijev felé, majd 1:09-től dróntámadásra is riasztást adtak ki. A mostani támadásra néhány nappal azután került sor, hogy augusztus 1-jén egy másik nagyszabású orosz ballisztikus rakétacsapás legalább kilenc ember életét követelte Kijevben, és több mint harmincan megsérültek. Ukrajna tovább támadja a Wildberries raktárait A Kijevet ért orosz légitámadással egy időben Ukrajna újabb oroszországi célpontokra mért dróncsapást . Ukrán drónok a Wildberries nevű nagy orosz online kereskedelmi vállalat egyik raktárát vették célba a tulai területen fekvő Alekszin városban. Alekszin mintegy 320 kilométerre északkeletre található az ukrán–orosz határtól. Tula kormányzója, Dmitrij Miljajev megerősítette, hogy szerdára virradóan ukrán drón csapódott be a térségben található Wildberries-létesítménybe, valamint más célpontokat is támadás ért. „Az előzetes információk szerint a venevi járásban két lakóépületben, valamint két ipari létesítményben – Novomoszkovszkban és az Uzlovszkij járásban – keletkeztek károk. Emellett egy drón a Wildberries egyik szortírozóközpontjának területére zuhant, ami tüzet okozott” – mondta a kormányzó. A Wildberries tulai raktárát ért legutóbbi támadás egy hosszabb ideje tartó csapássorozat része, amely az elmúlt hetekben Oroszország-szerte több Wildberries-logisztikai központot is érintett. A Wildberries weboldalán katonai felszerelések széles választéka is szerepel, köztük drónalkatrészek és golyóálló mellények is. Az orosz Amazonként is emlegetett vállalat banki érdekeltségét júliusban szankciókkal sújtotta az Európai Unió, mivel az EU szerint pénzügyi hozzájárulást nyújt Oroszország állami költségvetéséhez. https://www.theguardian.com/australia-ne.text: Overnight temperatures were close to freezing and Belgian backpacker Celine Cremer, 31, had insufficient clothing, including nothing waterproof, the coroner found. Photograph: Supplied by Tasmania police/AAP View image in fullscreen Overnight temperatures were close to freezing and Belgian backpacker Celine Cremer, 31, had insufficient clothing, including nothing waterproof, the coroner found. Photograph: Supplied by Tasmania police/AAP Tasmania ‘Confluence of errors’ led to Belgian tourist Celine Cremer’s death in Tasmanian wilderness, coroner finds Coroner finds 31-year-old deviated from a walking track as dusk fell, four days before the winter solstice Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Australian Associated Press Fri 28 Aug 2026 00.10 EDT Last modified on Fri 28 Aug 2026 04.11 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Overlapping errors, including a lack of preparation in near-freezing winter weather, contributed to the death of a Belgian tourist on a wilderness track. Celine Cremer set off on a walk at Philosopher Falls in Tasmania’s remote north-west on 17 June 2023 and was reported missing almost 10 days later. Extensive initial police efforts found no trace of the 31-year-old before private searches organised by her friends and family discovered her remains near a river in January 2026. In findings published on Friday, the coroner, Madeleine Wilson, ruled Cremer died between 17 and 21 June, 2023 as a result of an accident. Map Her death followed a “confluence of errors” that began when she took a walking track towards Magnet Dam after visiting the Philosopher Falls lookout. “The track to Magnet Dam was not well defined and she wandered off track and became lost,” Wilson said. “The deviation from the track occurred late in the day, four days before the winter solstice, at which time the afternoon light was starting to fade.” View image in fullscreen Searchers scoured wilderness in 2023 near the Philosopher Falls track in Tasmania in the hunt for Cremer. Her remains were found earlier this year. Photograph: Tasmania police Overnight temperatures in the area at the time were close to freezing and Cremer had insufficient clothing, including nothing waterproof, Wilson said. Phone reception was intermittent and she lost her mobile, which was her only form of communication, late in the afternoon on the day she set out. Her phone was found by a search party of volunteers in December 2025. Recovered data showed she took several photos and videos between 2.21pm and 2.42pm and used Google maps several times afterwards with the last input recorded at 4.18pm. It is likely Cremer got lost around 3.49pm and subsequently became disorientated without her phone and mistakenly changed direction, the coroner said. “It is not possible to determine the route taken once Cremer lost her mobile phone, to her final resting place in the Arthur River,” Wilson said. It was possible Cremer slipped and fell, or tried unsuccessfully to cross the river. Cremer had travelled to Australia in 2022 on a working holiday and was planning to return to the mainland four days after the Philosopher Falls walk. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Around 2-3 times a day Sign up to Breaking News US Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion Wilson praised the efforts of a private search company and volunteers which ultimately led to the first discovery of Cremer’s remains. The police response to the missing person report was appropriate and their search efforts were guided by “accepted methodologies”. Police efforts were somewhat limited by weather, Wilson said, noting water levels in the Arthur River were significantly higher in 2023 than when her remains were found. View image in fullscreen The car of then-missing Belgian tourist Celine Cremer in northwest Tasmania in 2023. Photograph: Tasmania police/AFP/Getty Images Tasmania Police has committed to a review into the use of private search groups in missing persons investigations, including consideration of formal protocols. Cremer failed to follow standard safety precautions, such as taking appropriate equipment and telling people where you are going, Wilson said. “Walkers should familiarise themselves with these standard safety messages before embarking on short walks, day walks or multi-day hikes,” she said. “Walkers should also be aware that mobile coverage is often intermittent or unavailable in remote areas of the Tasmanian wilderness and should plan accordingly.” Wilson recommended the local council put up signs at the entrance to the Philosopher Falls track, explaining it is not managed for recreational use and the surface is degraded, uneven and may be hazardous. https://www.theguardian.com/politics/liv.text: Morning, and welcome to our UK politics blog. The assisted dying bill is back in the Commons today, where MPs will vote on a proposal that would allow adults in England and Wales with less than six months to live to seek medical assistance to end their lives. MPs had previously voted through the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill, brought forward by Labour MP Kim Leadbeater, in June 2025, but it foundered in the House of Lords earlier this year after opponents tabled more than 1,280 amendments. Prime minister Andy Burnham has confirmed he will not vote, saying he does not want to “unduly influence the debate”. The bill has been revived by Labour MP Lauren Edwards, who said there was “a real human cost to the delay in passing this legislation and correcting the injustices and cruelty of the current law”. Two Labour MPs have also warned of “extraordinary risks” if ministers try to force the assisted dying bill using an obscure parliamentary procedure, should it continue to be block

https://www.pressenza.com/2026/09/ukrain.text: Search While the ruling liberal coalition might lament this emerging trend, no matter how statistically insignificant it is at present, the conservative and libertarian-nationalist opposition parties are probably pleased and might hope that the numbers grow much larger. Poland’s RMF24 cited the latest Eurostat data in early September to report that ~6,300 Ukrainian refugees left Poland in June followed by ~8,100 in July, so nearly a one-third increase over a single month, but these numbers are small compared to the ~953,100 Ukrainian refugees that are still in Poland. The larger context concerns the ongoing Polish-Ukrainian dispute that erupted in late May after Zelensky glorified the Volhynia Genocide ’s OUN-UPA culprits at the state level. Since then, some highly publicized incidents occurred between Poles and Ukrainians in Poland as the locals’ views about them soured as a result, which drew attention to what the ruling liberal coalition considers to be rising “hate crimes” against Ukrainians . Justice Minister Waldemar Żurek announced over the summer that over 100 prosecutors are working to convict Poles accused of such crimes, Prime Minister Donald Tusk condemned this alleged trend, and nationwide protests were organized against it. For whatever one thinks about all of this, and some Poles on social media have argued that Ukrainians provoked the locals in some of the highly publicized incidents in order to then film their reaction as a means of manipulating perceptions about what happened, it’s a major topic of discussion in Poland. Some Ukrainians might therefore truly believe, whether rightly or not, that they’re in danger if they remain in Poland and accordingly decided to leave for elsewhere in Europe. The alleged trend of rising “hate crimes” against Ukrainians aside, some Ukrainians might also have begun feeling more uncomfortable if some of the locals started treating them differently in everyday life as a result of the ongoing Polish-Ukrainian dispute, which could contribute to them leaving. Another factor might be that Ukrainians no longer enjoy special benefits in Poland like before after conservative President Karol Nawrocki, Tusk’s rival, abolished them earlier this year in accordance with his promise . While the ruling liberal coalition might lament the emerging trend of Ukrainians finally beginning to leave Poland, no matter how statistically insignificant it is at present, the conservative and libertarian-nationalist opposition parties are probably pleased and might hope that the numbers grow much larger. That’s because they’re increasingly aware of the security-related risks of a substantial Ukrainian minority being formed in what was one of the world’s most ethno-culturally homogenous countries before 2022. “ The Ukrainian Ambassador To Poland Admitted That His Co-Ethnics Don’t Want To Assimilate ” in September 2025, which was followed a month later by Ukrainian media talking about how “ An Ethnic Ukrainian Lobby Might Soon Take Shape In The Polish Sejm ”. Ukrainian nationalists also claim southeastern Poland , which recontextualizes the “ Project Trident ” anti-crime initiative as a dual preemptive anti-insurgency one. Less Ukrainians in Poland means less of a post-war threat from Ukraine . It’s premature to predict that the emerging trend of Ukrainians finally beginning to leave Poland will soon reach a meaningful level, let alone that most of them will ultimately leave instead of pursue a path to citizenship, but it’s still worth monitoring. If that’s indeed what happens, however, then it’s expected to become another partisan issue ahead of fall 2027’s next Sejm elections and figure into Ukraine’s anti-Polish propaganda since it’ll likely be blamed on the alleged trend of rising “hate crimes”.
